In Awen’s childhood memories, her home was just like any ordinary family home in Bloomville — simple, warm, and familiar. Back then, the biggest problem in her life seemed to be that her mother would stay out in the flower fields to cultivate new varieties instead of coming home, while her father’s complaints gave Awen no end of headaches.
Even when she sensed that she was somehow different from the other people of Bloomville, it never troubled her back then.
Except on those rare occasions when snow fell over the Sea of Flowers.
Her mother would gaze toward its deepest reaches, a wistful look in her eyes.
Young Awen asked her mother what lay beyond the Sea of Flowers.
Her mother only shook her head, as if there were things she couldn’t bring herself to speak about.
When Awen grew up, she found a line in her mother’s research notes — no context before it, none after.
"It’s snowing, but my homeland isn’t there anymore."
It was then that Awen understood — no wonder she carried a different scent from the people of Bloomville. She had another homeland somewhere.
She wanted to find that homeland, to find the "origin" she had never visited.
At last, after braving countless dangers, she reached the ancient white perfume tower deep within the Sea of Flowers, and found the perfume formula called "Homeland" — and with it, her origin.
She was from Azureville. She had never truly belonged here.
She thought: she had to leave this place and go toward her origin.
As for the perfume named "Homeland" — there was no need to bring it to her mother. Because the homeland in her mother’s heart was the white plateau, collapsed utterly in the upheaval of the earth — the place where she had lived alongside the Budsquires in her own childhood.
For some people, home is a guiding scent, leading toward the place they came from.
For others, home is a place one is destined to leave. To leave home is to begin anew.

Among the Budsquire family, Thornblades are guardians armed with unbreakable thorns.
To protect his little sister, one Budsquire brother became a mighty Thornblade. He challenged one famed Lethal Thorn after another, making the same pact each time: the loser would break off their own thorn.
But no Thornblade wins forever.
After his thorn was broken, he could not bear to be comforted by his sister, much less protected by her. So he ventured into a thunderstorm, hoping to become a stronger Thunderstorm Thornblade.
He failed.
After losing her brother, the little sister was no longer the innocent flower she once was. When her tears finally ran dry, she began her own training.
On a stormy night, she bloomed into a flower of grief, with thorns as cold and merciless as her pain.
Since then, she has cut down every challenger without hesitation, breaking their thorns without mercy.
Perhaps because that same cruel ritual took her brother from her. Perhaps because she despises the duels themselves.
Or perhaps she is still waiting for someone strong enough to defeat her—to take the Pale Thorn from her, and with it, finally set her free.
